match.reason: DFO salmon: THREE items. gnis:9630 Alouette River (mainstem) + gnis:39404 North Alouette River — DFO names the North Alouette explicitly ('above 216th Street, including the North Alouette River and tributaries to that part', and a whole reach 'North Alouette and tributaries') — + wbk:329292631, the river polygon on the mainstem that FWA mislabels 'South Alouette River' and name_variants renames. Alouette Lake (wbk:329291807) is NOT included: it is the reservoir above the dam and DFO's reaches are all river reaches (216th St, Allco Park, Pitt confluence). Every locator already has its cut-point: alouette_river__216_street_bridge, alouette_river__alouette_boundary_signs (Allco Park), alouette_river__216th_street on the North arm; the Pitt River confluence is a natural end.

DFO salmon: the row is named for the HATCHERY but the regulated water is the CHEHALIS RIVER (gnis:13015) — 'from the hatchery outlet downstream to the confluence with the Chehalis/Harrison Rivers'. Deliberately NOT a name_variants entry: 'Chehalis River Hatchery' is a facility, not a name for the river, and making it a searchable name of the water would be wrong. The upstream bound is the curated split chehalis_river__hatchery_outlet; the downstream bound is the river's natural mouth into the Harrison.

DFO salmon: FIVE registry items. The provincial synopsis already binds the first three as 'CHILLIWACK / VEDDER RIVERS (does not include Sumas River)' -> gnis 8634 + 3062 + 29662; DFO's row is that same system INCLUDING the Sumas, which is why it needs its own entry and why that entry is tagged source=dfo — the provincial row says the opposite in its own name. Sumas is TWO items: the stream (gnis:26216) and the lake polygon (wbk:328997872) the stream runs through. Sumas Lake Canal (gnis:6015 / wbk:329707192) is deliberately NOT included — DFO names the Sumas River. Both Sumas bounds already exist: 'Barrow Town Pump Station' is the auto lake boundary sumas_river__sumas_river (lake:328997872), and 'boundary signs near the confluence with the Fraser River' is the reach's NATURAL downstream end (section 356352298:0 drains straight into a Fraser node), so no split was minted for either.
